chunks: From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī; and from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah and al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, all from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying:

"Whoever kills a believer deliberately, retaliation is taken from him, unless the heirs of the slain are satisfied to accept the blood-money. If they are satisfied with the blood-money and the killer approves that, then the blood-money is twelve thousand, or one thousand dinars, or one hundred camels. If he is in a land where dinars are used, then one thousand dinars; if he is in a land where camels are used, then one hundred camels; and if he is in a land where dirhams are used, then dirhams according to the reckoning of twelve thousand."

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a gold coin standard used to quantify diyah
key_terms.قِيدَ مِنْهُ: retaliation is exacted from him in qisas
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believer whose intentional killing is being discussed
key_terms.ٱلدَّرَاهِمُ: silver dirhams used as a monetary standard for diyah
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةَ: blood-money paid in place of retaliation if accepted
key_terms.ٱلْإِبِلِ: camels used as a standard measure of diyah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intentional killing and diyah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for intentional killing of a believer: the default ruling is qisas (retaliation), unless the heirs of the victim agree to accept diyah. It also specifies the standard measures of diyah and indicates that the applicable form may follow the customary currency or property of the land.
